held_out_title: You asked me to roast your AI resumes.. so I did.
notes: The criteria are the general, checkable rules behind the reviewer's specific
criticisms, not the criticisms themselves. The reviewed resumes exist only as
pixels in the video and are in no corpus, so 'find the same faults in the same
document' is not a measurable thing; 'reach the same rules' is.
Every quote is verified against the chunk store at its own start_seconds by
src.evals.critique.verify_dataset, which the tests run. A criterion whose quote
cannot be found where it claims is a criterion the dataset's author invented.
applies_to marks which artifact kinds a rule can be checked against at all, and
every exclusion must carry a note giving its reason (enforced by a test). This
is the softest judgement in the file and it moves the headline: an independent
audit found that all six original exclusions removed criteria the system had
MISSED and none it had reached, worth +33% relative. It overturned c09. Read
criteria_recall_all beside criteria_recall — it is served and rendered for
exactly this reason, and it is immune to the choice.
group marks criteria that are the same rule said twice. One-to-one matching
means a system making one correct point about links can only ever satisfy one
of c12/c24, which is a recall ceiling unrelated to retrieval; the grouped
recall reports the score without that ceiling.

criteria.criterion: A resume should fit on a single page, even for an engineer with more than ten years of experience.
criteria.quote: you want to keep your resume to just a single page
criteria.note: Page count is a resume mechanic; a scrolling website has no equivalent.

criteria.criterion: Cut or reorder experience that is irrelevant to the role being targeted, instead of listing everything you have ever done.
criteria.quote: shuffle your experience around to make it make the most sense for the job application

criteria.criterion: Work should show clear individual ownership of what was built, not merely participation in a team that built it.
criteria.quote: there's clear ownership of the projects. It's not just about building something with a team

criteria.criterion: Keep the opening summary to two or three lines and do not restate there what the body of the document already proves.
criteria.quote: reduce their professional summary to just two to three lines

criteria.criterion: Put explicit numbers on claims of scale or reliability rather than leaving the reader to take the claim on trust.
criteria.quote: be a little bit more explicit about how many releases there actually were

criteria.criterion: There must be a visible career narrative that leads from the previous roles into the role now being applied for.
criteria.quote: there is no clear story that leads this person into AI engineering

criteria.criterion: Build one flagship project in the target domain that bridges the existing professional experience to the job being sought.
criteria.quote: they don't have their own North Star project to showcase in the resume, there isn't a clear bridge

criteria.criterion: Limit any one role to about three bullet points, however long that role lasted.
criteria.quote: limit the bullet points here to a maximum of three
criteria.note: About the bullet list under an employment entry, which a project portfolio does not have.

criteria.criterion: Compress older roles to one or two lines rather than removing them, so the years of experience still show without consuming space.
criteria.quote: you can optimize one or two lines in each of these sections and just keep them brief

criteria.criterion: Drop courses and credentials that add nothing for the target role, because the skill should be evident from the work instead.
criteria.quote: I don't know what the added value is of this online course on training great tech leaders

criteria.criterion: Do not carry a separate skills list that repeats what the described work already demonstrates.
criteria.quote: remove the skill section altogether because your skills will be very obvious from the work experience itself

criteria.criterion: Include links to your profiles and code so a reader can independently check that the projects are real.
criteria.quote: links to LinkedIn, GitHub and actually a way to check out the validity of the projects mentioned

criteria.criterion: Cut vague competence claims that could be said of anyone in the role and that the employment history already implies.
criteria.quote: these kinds of fluffy sentences are really just a waste of the potential recruiter's attention

criteria.criterion: A recruiter gives the document twenty to thirty seconds, so the most convincing material has to be reachable immediately.
criteria.quote: You really want to make sure that they get to the meat of your resume as soon as possible

criteria.criterion: Order the document so the strongest project sits at the very top, above any list of technologies.
criteria.quote: put your top project, your North Star project, at the very top

criteria.criterion: Describe a project concretely enough that the underlying skills are self-evident, instead of asserting the skills separately.
criteria.quote: skills like being able to build scalable solutions will be obvious from the project description alone

criteria.criterion: Check the document for stale statements left over from an earlier version, such as naming the wrong target role.
criteria.quote: I assume that this is kind of from a previous version of the resume, but double-check these kinds of things

criteria.criterion: Keep the document in a plain-text source format such as LaTeX or markdown so it can be machine-checked before each application.
criteria.quote: resume should be written in a format like LaTeX or a markdown file
criteria.note: A reviewer of a published site sees only the rendered output, so there is no source document for them to judge. (The earlier reason given here — that a website has no plain-text source — was simply wrong for a GitHub Pages site.)

criteria.criterion: Reframe the earlier career as the foundation the target-domain work is built on, rather than as unrelated prior history.
criteria.quote: reframed where the data infrastructure fundamentals that this person has is a foundation for the AI pipelines

criteria.criterion: Keep the education section to a single line once you have been working for years.
criteria.quote: the education section is very slim here. It's just a single line
criteria.note: The portfolio has no education section to keep to a line.

criteria.criterion: Put certifications inside the experience they apply to and deep-link the proof, instead of listing them on their own line.
criteria.quote: add a deep link to a certification platform where it shows the proof that you got that certification
criteria.note: About where certifications sit inside an employment history; the portfolio lists no certifications.

criteria.criterion: Aim the whole document at one clear role persona and build everything else around it.
criteria.quote: You want to aim for one clear role persona and build the rest of your resume around that

criteria.criterion: Cut corporate jargon and reduce the volume of prose, because too much text crowds out the actual evidence.
criteria.quote: there's a lot of corporate jargon because essentially we are trained to use corporate jargon

criteria.criterion: Every project mentioned should carry a link to the artifact itself so a reader can verify it exists.
criteria.quote: none of them have an embedded link to a GitHub page
